correctness.rationale: The proof derives necessary bundle sizes from strict positivity; for four goods it proves iff \(a\le b+c\) via exact two-center EFX inequalities. For five goods it shows the double bundle can contain a globally smallest good, reduces EFX to two inequalities, and proves the iff \(a\le b+c\)+e via two exhaustive cases. The insertion-rank argument isolates losses to new maxima; ordered-spacing Laplace transforms give both exact joint laws. A direct separate allocation checker enumerates all complete assignments on 791 integer profiles and 600 rational profiles, and exact Fraction arithmetic verifies both matrices. Finite enumeration is auxiliary, not presented as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest equivalent group fairness formulation is equal-weight g-WEFX of Scarlett–Teh–Zick (2023), and Deligkas et al. (2026) use the same two-level fairness notions. Both provide unbalanced four-good nonexistence examples; neither gives the iff conditions for all cardinal four- and five-good profiles, the one-sided nonmaximum insertion property, or either exact coupled distribution. Broader NP-hardness and positive guarantees for weaker group EF1 do not imply the proposed exact EFX classifications. Focused literature and mathematical-record searches disclosed no equivalent statement; this is evidence-limited originality, not a uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: Equivalent calculations could exist in unindexed appendices, unpublished notes or later research not returned by the inspected searches.

The event probabilities can be reframed as classical order-statistic inequalities; those underlying order-statistic integrals may have appeared independently, though no source was found implying the two-level allocation equivalence and joint transition law.

value.rationale: The smallest four-good obstruction to simultaneous center-EFX and global agent-EF1 is already a central example in the motivating literature. Exact four/five-good feasibility thresholds settle the next natural cardinal cells, while the nonmaximum-addition monotonicity and positive loss/rescue events reveal a genuine resource-monotonicity paradox for existence. The complete coupled probabilities under two standard priors quantify how sensitive feasibility is to valuation tails and can guide future random-instance and mechanism benchmarks. It does not rely on unmotivated parameter slicing or a negligible numerical improvement.
